claims.assertion: There is a single off-route segment, F3 (12:46–13:07), in which 9.70 km were driven where the optimal route covers 5.62 km, adding 4.08 km and reaching up to 1720 m from the optimal route; fares are computed only on this segment's extra_km.

The driver's written statement that he followed his GPS off at Paya Lebar (F8) is a post-trip statement that cannot supply consent, since consent must be a rider message sent before the segment starts and the chat contains none (F7).

This is an undiscounted metered RydeTAXI trip (surge 1.0x, F5) billed $42.52 by distance and time (20.08 km, 34.0 min, F6), so the refund measure in RD-2 is the excess kilometres only, not the whole fare.

The fare record quantifies the excess at $6.50 for 4.61 km at $1.4099/km (F4), which is the per-kilometre rate derived from this trip's distance fare of $28.31 over 20.08 km (F6), and that $6.50 is the maximum exposure on the off-route segment.

points.response: Conceded: the record shows one off-route segment only, F3 (12:46–13:07, +4.08 km, up to 1720 m off the optimal route), and my case is built on that single segment; it is nonetheless an unexempted detour under RD-1.

Conceded: the chat record is empty (F7), so no rider message predates the segment and its correct ground is consent_after_or_none, not an agreed route; that is exactly what makes the segment unexempted under RD-5 and RD-1.
Conceded: the driver's post-trip statement (F8) cannot supply consent, which under RD-5 must be the rider's own message sent before the segment starts — and none exists (F7).

Conceded: the traffic test fails — no incidents near the route in the trip window (F12), PIE at band 7, 60–69 km/h (F10), fair weather (F13) — so no RD-4 reasonable cause exists and the segment falls to RD-2.

Agreed as to the measure: this is a metered RydeTAXI trip (F5, F6), so RD-2 refunds the unexempted segment's extra kilometres only, which is precisely the relief I seek; the rider's 200 m-corridor and map-jitter mileage is not claimed.

Not disputed on quantum: F4 quantifies the excess at $6.50 (4.61 km × $1.4099/km, the rate derived from F6's $28.31 over 20.08 km), and the driver's own brief agrees that $6.50 is the exposure on the off-route segment.

Conceded: nothing in the chat (F7) or the driver's statement (F8) reads as a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation is required.

Conceded as a record: F1 (20.1 km vs 15.5 km optimal, +4.6 km/+30%) and F2 (34.0 min vs 21.8 min) are true, but they are trip aggregates; under RD-1 liability attaches segment by segment, and the only recorded segment is F3 with 4.08 km of added distance, so the aggregates cannot enlarge the refund beyond that segment.
Accepted: F3 is the sole off-route segment (9.70 km driven vs 5.62 km optimal, +4.08 km, up to 1720 m off route) and it is unexempted, so a mileage refund on that segment is due.

Agreed on the record: F7 shows the chat is empty and F3 starts at 12:46, so there was no rider message before the segment — the ground is consent_after_or_none under RD-5, not an implied or verbal agreement.

F8 is my client's own post-trip statement and I do not rely on it as consent or as a defence; it does not, however, add any fact to F3, so it cannot support anything beyond the segment already measured.

Not disputed as far as it goes: F12 records no incidents near the route, F10 shows the PIE at band 7 (60–69 km/h) through 12:46, and F9 shows the CTE at band 7 during 12:30–13:15, so no RD-4 exemption is available and I do not press one; F11 (Paya Lebar Road, band 4) concerns the road driven, not the replaced optimal-route leg, and I do not rely on it.

The measure under RD-2 is extra_km of the unexempted segment, i.e. 4.08 km from F3, not the 4.61 km billed in F4; the difference (about $0.75 at the $1.4099/km rate in F4) is corridor and map-matching mileage which RD-2 expressly does not refund, so the maximum is $5.75, not $6.50.
Accepted: F6 shows the waiting fee was $0.00 and F5 shows surge 1.0×, so the only live item is the mileage element on F3.

F15 (5 disputes, 3 upheld, all route) may support flag_account under RD-6 as an additional action, but profile facts cannot decide whether this trip's deviation was unjustified; on the segment the outcome follows from F3 alone, and I do not contest the $6.50-based refund of the mileage element of RD-2 — I ask for it at the segment figure of $5.75.
